newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: State-owned Bank of Ceylon to cut lending rate.
newsitem.headline: State-owned Bank of Ceylon to cut lending rate.

text.p: The State-owned Bank of Ceylon said it will cut interest rates from February 1, in response to a monetary policy relaxation by the Central Bank earlier this month.
"We will reduce interest rates by one percent in direct response to the Central Bank's moves earlir this month," a senior Bank of Ceylon official told Reuters.
The Central Bank cut statutory reserves to 14 percent from 15 on local currency depsoits, and removed a five percent statutory requirement on foreign currency desposits placed abroad.
In addition, exporters were also permitted foreign currency borrowings.
The rate cut would initially see a significant fall in the bank's earnings, the official said.
"A one percent reduction in interest rates alone should see a decline in earnings of about 300 to 400 million rupees," he said.
But when viewed in the context of the volume of rupees that will be freed when exporters borrow in foreign currency, the fall should be minimised in the medium term, he added.
"The bank will have additional rupees for lending," he said.
The Central Bank said it expected the recent relaxation to increase lending capacity of commercial banks by about 10 billion rupees or five percent.
Since the Bank of Ceylon has a 25 percent market share of all advances, it was setting the standard, the official said.
"I think it is in everyone's interest to work towards a low interest rate scenario, and we are giving the lead," he said.
